analysis: Examined scripts/test-release-dev-branch.py base and head. These are offline trust-scope tests that reflect a rewrite of the dev-branch release lane. Base: the lane was dispatch-only and ad-hoc signed. Base lines 60-68 barred the Developer ID, notarization and APPLE_* secrets, lines 94-100 kept the build job secret-free, and lines 87-92 had publication run from master. Head: a push to dev is the only trigger (lines 96-103). The caller job runs the local reusable release-provider.yml with environment dev and `secrets: inherit` (lines 120-140). Within the reusable workflow, signing uses the Developer ID and notarization (lines 200-212). Apple secrets are read only in build-and-release, and prod/staging secrets are read only behind an expression guard (lines 179-198). Line 198 asserts no GitHub environment is attached to any lane. The resulting regression, which gives dev-branch code access to all secrets, is reported as a finding. Unverified contracts that integration must check: (1) the actual .github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml and release-provider.yml contents, which are not in this batch; (2) branch protection on dev versus master; (3) whether PROD_* secrets are repo- or org-level rather than environment-scoped; (4) whether qualification and official-build checks bind to full CodeDirectory/CDHash identity (A-017, T-054) rather than Team ID, so that a Developer ID-signed dev build cannot pass as qualified. The `-dev.branch.` marker and the installer's dev identity selection were previously pinned by the base version-string test. The head test removes that pin (except in run-name, line 150), so marker separation should be verified elsewhere. The test only parses the checked-out files and does not gate the triggering run.

findings.detail: The head tests now require the caller to run the pushed commit's own `./.github/workflows/release-provider.yml` with `secrets: inherit` (lines 126-127, 137). They also require that the reusable workflow attach no GitHub `environment:` for prod, staging or dev (line 198), so prod and staging secrets are not environment-protected. Prod and staging secrets are separated only by an expression guard inside that same file (GUARDED_SECRET, lines 41-43). That file comes from the dev commit that triggered the run. These offline tests cannot stop the triggering run from executing a modified copy. Base kept dev-branch code credential-free: lines 94-100 required no secret in the build job, and lines 87-92 required publishing from master-checked-out scripts. Base lines 60-68 also barred the Apple signing identity. Trigger: anyone who can push to `dev` commits a release-provider.yml that reads PROD_* secrets without the guard, or misuses APPLE_CERTIFICATE_P12. Impact: exposure of production release-publication keys (A-005) and of the Developer ID signing and notarization identity. An attacker could then publish or register untrusted binaries (A-011) or obtain Apple-signed, notarized builds of arbitrary dev code that carry the production team identity (T-013, T-054). Fix: scope prod and staging secrets to protected GitHub environments with branch restrictions. Pass only the needed secrets explicitly instead of `inherit`. Alternatively, require `dev` to have master-equivalent branch protection and use a distinct signing identity for dev.
findings.title: Dev-push lane hands every repository secret, including Developer ID signing material, to dev-branch workflow code
